events.title: First Observed Transit of Venus
events.description: English astronomers Jeremiah Horrocks and William Crabtree made the first successful observations of Venus crossing the face of the Sun. Each watched from his own home and recorded the event.
events.significance: Their observations helped refine estimates of the size of the solar system. They also began a tradition of transit-watching that guided astronomy for centuries.

events.title: Sati Banned in British India
events.description: Governor-General Lord William Bentinck issued a regulation outlawing sati, the custom of a widow's self-immolation on her husband's funeral pyre, in British-ruled territories. Reformer Ram Mohan Roy had campaigned for years for the ban.
events.significance: The ban was a landmark in Indian social reform. It showed how local reform movements and colonial authority could combine to end a deadly practice.

events.title: The Mary Celeste Is Found Adrift
events.description: The American brigantine Mary Celeste was found apparently abandoned in the Atlantic. Her cargo was largely intact, and no one aboard was ever found.
events.significance: The ship became one of history's most enduring mysteries. It remains the standard example of a ghost ship.

events.title: Led Zeppelin Disbands
events.description: The English rock band officially announced its breakup. The decision followed the death of drummer John Bonham earlier that year.
events.significance: The band chose to end rather than carry on without Bonham. Its influence on hard rock and heavy metal is still felt today.

events.title: Pan Am Ceases Operations
events.description: Pan American World Airways shut down after 64 years in the air. It had been the leading American international airline for much of the 20th century.
events.significance: The collapse closed a chapter in the history of commercial flight. Pan Am had helped make long-distance air travel a part of ordinary life.
